blocks.text: Gmail on a Mac runs in your browser
Most producers reach Gmail on a Mac through a browser tab. Open gmail.com in Safari or Chrome, then sign in with your Google Account. Google's sign-in help says the same for computers.

The Google pages we checked describe the browser version only. Third-party sites say no Gmail app exists for Mac, but we could not confirm that on a Google page. Treat the browser as your Mac version for now.

Each browser keeps its own sign-in. If you run two Google accounts, check which one a tab uses before you send a lease or an invoice. A wrong account is an easy slip when two accounts share one browser.
Pin Gmail to the Dock with Safari
Safari can turn a website into a web app in the Dock. The web app opens in its own window, so Gmail stays out of your browser tabs during a session.

items: Open gmail.com in Safari and sign in.
Click Share in the Safari toolbar.
Choose Add to Dock, then click Add.

blocks.text: Apple's Safari guide says that if you were signed in to the website, you are automatically signed in to the web app in most cases. Still, glance at the account before you send anything.
Apple's page does not give a minimum macOS version for web apps. If a step looks different on your screen, check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.
Set up templates for lease and invoice replies
Producers answer the same questions every week. Buyers ask what they can do with a beat. Studios ask for invoices and session details. Templates save one good reply and reuse it.
Google's Workspace help page covers the setup. You turn templates on first, under Settings. After that, saving and inserting takes two clicks.

items: Open Settings > See all settings > Advanced.
Select Enable in the Templates section.
Write the reply in a new message. Then click More > Templates > Save draft as template.
Next time, open a new message and click More > Templates > Insert template.

blocks.text: Templates can include your signature. Set that up first with the signature guide, so every reply ends the same way.

Two limits matter. Templates work only in Gmail on the web, so the mobile apps do not show them. Google's page also does not state a maximum number of templates. Some third-party sites give a cap, but we could not verify it, so do not plan around a number.
Track beat leases so receipts do not get lost

Lease tracking is where producer email gets messy. Feedtracks, a vendor that sells beat-licensing software, describes the pattern. Producers rely on email folders, PayPal receipts and BeatStars dashboards to track leases.
The post puts the problem in one line: 'You don't know if you've leased a beat 5 times or 50 times.' Read it as a sales pitch with a real problem behind it, since the vendor sells its own tool.
It also gives one example. A $49.99 beat was leased to 47 artists in a month. That is an illustration from one vendor, not a study. It still shows how fast receipts pile up.

Gmail can carry part of this load. Make one label for each sales platform, such as PayPal or BeatStars. Then make a filter that sends matching receipts to that label. The label guide and the filter guide show the clicks.
Search still helps, but it has limits. Feedtracks warns about searching through thousands of emails 'hoping you tagged everything correctly.' Labels shrink the search before you type anything.

blocks.text: Attachment limits for stems and contracts
Gmail caps attachments at 25 MB for personal accounts, according to Google's Gmail Help page. That fits a contract and a few MP3 previews. A full set of WAV stems can pass that limit quickly.

Workspace accounts follow different rules. The Workspace admin page lists 25 MB for Business, Education and Enterprise Standard, and up to 50 MB for Enterprise Plus. Those limits apply to web Gmail only.
If you send from a studio domain, ask your admin which tier you use. The limit comes from the account, not from your Mac.
The safer habit is a link. Put the stems in a shared folder, then paste the link into the email. The recipient gets the files, and your message stays small. The attachment guide covers the steps.
Sending limits when one drop goes to many artists
A beat drop to a long list is a bulk job, not a normal reply. Google Workspace allows 2,000 messages per day per user. Mail merge gets 1,500. Trial accounts get 500.
On Gmail web, one message can reach 2,000 total recipients, with no more than 500 external. Over SMTP or IMAP and POP clients, the cap is 100 recipients per message.
Workspace also caps total recipients at 10,000 per day. If you hit a sending limit, Workspace blocks sending for up to 24 hours. That pause can cost you a release day.
Split a long list into smaller batches. Log each batch with a sent label, so you know who got the drop and who did not.
Consumer Gmail limits were not on the pages we checked. Do not assume they match the Workspace numbers.
Find an old contract or receipt by search
Search beats scrolling when you know a file exists. Gmail accepts search operators in the search box. The attachment operator is the one producers need most.

Worked example. A buyer says they never got the exclusive license. Type from:buyer@example.com has:attachment in the search box, then open the newest PDF. Check the thread for the signed version, not a draft.
Narrow the search with date operators, such as after: and before:. The search guide for attachments shows the full list of filters you can use.
How Lazur helps you work inside Gmail
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud.

Three modes cover most Gmail questions. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Ask for text, and Lazur drafts it.
Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It is not a plugin for Gmail or any other app. Your hand does the clicking, which keeps you in control of what gets sent.
Dictate replies at the cursor with fn
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. That includes the Gmail compose box and the reply field under a thread.
Teach the personal dictionary your studio words. Add plugin names, sample pack names and buyer names. Spelling them once saves a fix in every email.
Snippets hold text you reuse, such as a licensing line or a sign-off. Clipboard slots keep copied items ready to paste. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
Ask Lazur to read and draft a licensing thread
Long threads are where licensing details hide. Ask Lazur what the buyer wants. It answers out loud from the thread on your screen.
Then ask for a draft. Lazur types it into the compose box, in the words you choose. Read every line before you click Send, because that click is yours.
Keep the question narrow. Ask what usage this buyer is requesting, not what you should do. A narrow question gets an answer you can check against the thread.
Lazur sees what is on your screen while you hold the shortcut. Anything outside that window stays out of the conversation unless you open it.
Research licensing and sync contacts in the background
Background research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It returns a summary and a report when it finishes.
Give it a clear brief. For example: find the submission terms for three sync agencies, then list the rights each one asks for and the page where you found them.
Check each claim on the source page before you email anyone. Research speeds up the search. It does not replace reading the agreement.
Reminders and calendar work from your voice
Everyday tasks include timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume. Producers use these between sessions, when the inbox is open and the mix is not.
Say 'remind me to send the invoice Friday afternoon.' Lazur adds it to Apple Reminders. Say 'add a calendar event for the mix review Thursday' and it adds one to Calendar.
Mistakes producers make in Gmail

items: Trusting search alone for lease history. Labels catch what search misses.
Attaching full stem packs and hitting the 25 MB limit. Use a shared link instead.
Retyping the same licensing answer. Save it once as a template.
Sending from the wrong account in the Dock web app. Check the account first.
Sending one large drop without checking Workspace limits. Split the list.
Expecting templates on your phone. They work only on the web.

blocks.text: Privacy: what Lazur hears and sends
Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask, the audio and a screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. Those are not stored.
Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on the Mac.
For Gmail, close other sensitive windows before you hold the shortcut. A screenshot captures everything on screen, not only the thread you want help with.
Mac requirements and what Lazur does not do
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.
Lazur does not operate other apps for you. It does not click buttons, edit files or send mail. Some Gmail jobs still need your hands on the mouse.
Gmail itself stays in the browser. Lazur works alongside it, not inside it, and it is not an add-in for any app.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: The Google pages we checked describe Gmail in a browser. For an app-like window, add Gmail to the Dock with Safari. Third-party sites say no Mac app exists, but we could not confirm that on a Google page.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my phone?
faq.answer: No. Google says templates work only in Gmail on the web. The Gmail mobile apps do not show them, so save and insert replies from a browser on your Mac.

faq.question: How big can an attachment be in Gmail?
faq.answer: For personal Gmail, the attachment limit is 25 MB. For Google Workspace web sending, the limit is 25 MB for Business, Education and Enterprise Standard, and 50 MB for Enterprise Plus. Send bigger stems as shared links.

faq.question: How many emails can I send in a day?
faq.answer: Google Workspace allows 2,000 messages per day per user. Trial accounts get 500. Consumer Gmail limits were not on the pages we checked, so check Google's current help before a big send.

faq.question: Can Lazur send my email or click Send?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons for you. It can guide you one click at a time, point at Send, or draft text for you to review before you send.

faq.question: Does Lazur listen to me all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Gmail specifically?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app because it sees your screen while you hold the shortcut. It is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail or any other app, and it does not operate Gmail for you.
